answers.answer: Shuffle Factory cards, randomly select number of players + 1 face-down onto the board, and return the rest to the box without looking. Place one encounter token on each of the 11 marked territories. Randomly choose one structure bonus tile and place it face-up below the Popularity Track. The lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.
answers.evidence: Setup: ‘randomly select number of players + 1’; ‘one encounter token on each of the 11 marked territories’; ‘one structure bonus tile’; ‘lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.’

answers.answer: On each Faction Mat, set starting power and draw starting combat cards as indicated; put the character on the home base, one worker on each of the two land-adjoined territories adjoining it, four mechs over their abilities, and six stars by the emblem. On each Player Mat, set starting popularity and take starting coins and two objective cards as indicated; put six technology cubes on marked green boxes, four structures on matching boxes, four recruits on bottom-row circular spaces, and six remaining workers on Produce's red rectangles. The summary says the Faction Mat supplies starting power/combat-card instructions and the Player Mat supplies popularity, coins and objectives; exact player-specific amounts are unsupported here.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 3–4: ‘Faction Mat: set starting power and draw starting combat cards as indicated’; ‘Player Mat: set starting popularity and take starting coins and objectives as indicated (two objective cards).’

answers.answer: You must move the action token to a different section, but may take neither action, either action, or both; the top action must precede the bottom, and you cannot return to the top after doing the bottom. Rusviet may repeat a section, including its Factory card. Gains from the top row may pay the bottom-row cost. Pay all exposed red-box costs before the action; green boxes show benefits, which may be taken as much or as little as desired. Bottom costs and coin benefits vary by Player Mat and upgrades. If unable to afford an action, you may take a dead turn by moving the token and taking neither action; never pay only part of a cost.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: ‘different section from last turn’; ‘optionally take that section's top action once, then optionally its bottom action once’; ‘First pay the full cost’; ‘You may use top-row gains to pay the bottom-row cost.’

answers.answer: An enemy worker alone on your structure's territory controls that territory and its resources. Enemy units cannot use your structure's abilities; you retain the abilities even without control, except an uncontrolled Mill cannot produce. Pay action resource costs using resources from any territories you currently control, even when acting elsewhere.
answers.evidence: Control, resources and home bases: ‘An enemy worker alone on your structure's territory controls it and all its resources’; ‘Enemy units do not gain your structure's abilities’; ‘Pay costs using resources from any territories you currently control.’

answers.answer: No. A normal Move selects up to two different units, each moving one adjacent territory, and one unit cannot use both selections to move twice. A carried worker's transport does not count as its own movement, so it may subsequently move itself; likewise a worker may move onto a mech and be carried by that mech's later move. All unit types (characters, mechs, workers) can carry any number of resources; only mechs can also carry any number of your workers, never your character.
answers.evidence: Move OR coins: ‘move up to two different units, one adjacent territory each’; ‘cannot use both selections to move the same unit twice’; ‘Being carried does not count as the worker's own movement’; ‘Only mechs may also carry any number of your workers.’

answers.answer: A character or mech entering a territory with only enemy workers stops and cannot move again that turn. Those workers immediately retreat to their home base, leaving resources; lose one popularity per worker, down to zero. Insufficient popularity does not stop the retreat. This is not combat. A worker cannot independently move into enemy-worker-controlled territory.
answers.evidence: Move: ‘Your character/mech entering enemy workers only stops’; workers ‘immediately retreat to their home base, leaving resources’; ‘Lose one popularity per worker, down to zero’; ‘A worker cannot independently enter enemy-worker-controlled territory.’

answers.answer: After all units finish moving in the Move action, resolve any combat before the bottom-row action; the attacker chooses the order when there are multiple combats. Workers cannot independently move into or out of a territory controlled by enemy characters/mechs.
answers.evidence: Move: finish moving the other units, then resolve all combats ‘before the bottom-row action’; ‘attacker chooses multiple-combat order’; workers cannot independently move ‘into or out of’ enemy character/mech-controlled territory.

answers.answer: Bolster costs $1 and gives two power or one combat card, before upgrades; a built Monument also gives one popularity. Trade costs $1 and gives any two resources (same or different) or one popularity, before upgrades; a built Armory also gives one power. Traded resources must be placed on a controlled territory containing at least one worker. If all your workers are at home, you cannot Trade for resources, though the popularity choice remains available. If the combat deck is empty, shuffle discards into a new deck; if both deck and discard pile are empty, draw none.
answers.evidence: Bolster: ‘Pay $1, gain two power OR one combat card’; Trade: ‘Pay $1, gain any two resources ... OR one popularity’; resources go ‘on a controlled territory containing at least one worker’; combat deck rule: shuffle discards, but if both empty draw none.

answers.answer: Before producing, pay every exposed Produce cost, including any power, popularity and/or coins; you must be able to afford all of it. Choose up to two different controlled territories, and each worker there may produce one token on its own territory. New workers come from the Player Mat left to right after payment and are put in the producing village. You may decline some or all production, including new workers. Newly exposed costs apply to future Produce actions, not the cost already paid.
answers.evidence: Produce: ‘Pay every exposed Produce cost ... before producing’; ‘choose up to two different controlled territories’; ‘Take new workers from the Player Mat left to right, after payment’; exposed costs affect ‘future Produce actions.’

answers.answer: Upgrade costs oil: move any technology cube from a green box to an empty bracketed red box, improving a top benefit and reducing a bottom cost; solid-black-bordered red boxes cannot be upgraded. Deploy costs metal: put any mech on a controlled territory with your worker, never a lake. Its uncovered ability applies from then on to your character and every mech, not workers. Even after completing all upgrades, mechs, structures and recruits, you may still pay for that bottom action to gain its coins and applicable ongoing recruit bonuses. The precise resource quantities and coin amounts are mat-specific and unsupported by the summary.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row actions: ‘Upgrade — oil’; ‘Deploy — metal’; Deploy requires ‘a controlled territory with your worker, never a lake’; ‘may still pay for that bottom action to gain coins and applicable ongoing recruit bonuses.’

answers.answer: Build costs wood and places a structure on a controlled territory containing your worker. Only one structure total may be built per territory, including opponents' structures; the Factory is allowed, lakes and home bases are forbidden. Structures cannot move or be destroyed. A controlled Mill supplies an extra bonus production territory and produces as one worker; it can work without an actual worker there, but only while you control it. A Mine is your personal tunnel for all your unit movement, including Factory Move, even if an enemy controls the Mine's territory.
answers.evidence: Build: ‘controlled territory with your worker’; ‘Structures cannot be moved or destroyed’; Mill works ‘only while controlled’; Mine is a personal tunnel ‘even when enemy-controlled.’

answers.answer: For Enlist, take a recruit from any bottom-row section of your Player Mat, put it permanently on any open one-time recruit bonus on your Faction Mat, and immediately gain the chosen bonus: two power, two coins, two popularity, or two combat cards. The ongoing bonus is the circle uncovered where the recruit was removed, regardless of which one-time bonus you chose. For the rest of the game, when you, your immediate left neighbor, or immediate right neighbor takes the corresponding bottom-row action, the recruit owner may gain its exposed circle bonus; top actions, encounters and similar Factory actions do not trigger it. Resolve active player first, then left, then right, stopping if the sixth star ends play. In a two-player game, the opponent triggers the bonus once, not twice. The exact bottom-row bonus corresponding to each recruit location is mat-specific and unsupported here.
answers.evidence: Enlist and Ongoing recruits: recruit goes on ‘any open one-time recruit bonus’; ‘two power, two coins, two popularity, or two combat cards’; ongoing bonus is ‘the circle uncovered where you removed the recruit’; resolve ‘active player first, then left, then right’; two-player opponent triggers once.

answers.answer: Each combatant secretly chooses dial power from 0 up to the lesser of seven and current power, and may add up to one combat card per participating character/mech, even with zero dial power. Rusviet People's Army grants one additional combat card if any workers are present. If both players have combat mech abilities, attacker resolves theirs first, then defender. Reveal simultaneously and add dial and card values; both pay their dial power from the power track, while card values are temporary and do not cost track power. Attacker wins ties.
answers.evidence: Combat steps: dial ‘0 to the smaller of seven and your current power’; ‘one combat card per participating character/mech’; attacker mech abilities ‘first, then defender’; ‘attacker wins ties’; both pay dial power.

answers.answer: The winner controls the territory and resources and places a combat star if eligible (normally at most two combat stars; Saxony has no usual limit, up to six total stars). All losing characters, mechs and workers retreat to their home base, leaving all resources on the battle territory; Nordic Seaworthy may instead retreat eligible units and carried workers to adjacent lakes. A winning attacker loses one popularity for each enemy worker forced to retreat, even workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake; a winning defender loses none. Polania Camaraderie provides the stated exception for an aggressor winning on its turn. The loser draws one combat card if they revealed at least one power on the dial or through cards; a zero-total loser draws none.
answers.evidence: Combat steps 4–5: losing units ‘all characters, mechs and workers’ retreat, leaving ‘all resources’; attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker; loser draws one card if they revealed power on dial or through cards.

answers.answer: After the whole Move action and all combats, resolve an encounter if the character remains in the token territory; then discard the token and draw a card before a following bottom action. If contested entry is lost, the character retreats and the encounter token stays. Resources, workers, mechs and structures gained go to the encounter territory. Pay the encounter option's printed cost, but no additional normal action costs apply and no additional mat benefits, including ongoing recruit bonuses, are gained.
answers.evidence: Encounters: after ‘the whole Move action and all combats’; if entry is lost ‘the token stays’; gains go to ‘the encounter territory’; ‘Pay no additional normal action costs’ and gain no mat benefits or ongoing recruit bonuses.

answers.answer: Each player's character, on its first finish of a Move action at the Factory (after winning combat if necessary), must look at the available Factory cards, choose one, and return the rest; this applies to every player, not just the first visitor. Each player gets at most one permanent card, and later visits cannot exchange it. The card is a fifth action section with optional top then bottom, subject to the usual no-repeat rule (Rusviet exception). Factory actions do not give corresponding Player Mat coins, structure bonuses or ongoing recruit bonuses. Its bottom action moves one unit up to two territories within that Move action, or three for a character/mech with Speed; Mine access and normal movement/stop rules apply.
answers.evidence: Factory: ‘Every player's character’ on its first finish of a Move action there chooses a card; ‘at most one permanent card’; bottom moves one unit two territories, or three with Speed for character/mech.

answers.answer: Only on your own turn, before or after completing a top or bottom action, may you reveal a completed objective; you may wait, but must meet all requirements at the moment of reveal. Place the objective star and put both objective cards on the bottom of their deck. Normally a player scores only one objective star; Saxony retains the other card and can score both. Exact objective requirements depend on the cards and are unsupported by this summary.
answers.evidence: Objectives: reveal ‘on your own turn, before or after’ an action; meet ‘all requirements at the moment of reveal’; put ‘both objective cards on the bottom’; Saxony ‘retains the other card and can score both.’

answers.answer: Stars are earned for six upgrades, four deployed mechs, four built structures, four recruits, all eight workers on the board, one revealed completed objective, a combat victory (up to two stars), 18 popularity, or 16 power. Each goal is awarded once except the two combat stars and Saxony's exception. Other players' stars never block a goal. A placed star is permanent even if power or popularity later falls. The sixth star ends the game immediately, with no equalizing turns or further actions.
answers.evidence: Stars and immediate end lists all nine thresholds; ‘Other players' stars never block a goal’; ‘A placed star is permanent’; ‘sixth star immediately ends play.’

answers.answer: If a bottom-row action earns the sixth star, first collect its primary benefit, coins and your ongoing recruit benefit, then place that star. Neighbor power/popularity recruit stars are resolved only after the active player finishes the action, in active/left/right order, and only if no earlier sixth star ended the game. If units remain intermingled in an unresolved battle, undo that part of movement, returning initiating units to their origin territories; do not resolve another combat.
answers.evidence: Stars: collect ‘primary benefit, coins and your ongoing recruit benefit before placing that star’; neighbor stars occur ‘only after the active player finishes the action’; unresolved battle movement is undone.

answers.answer: At 10 popularity, each star is worth $4, each controlled territory $3, and each complete pair of controlled resources $2. Thus five stars add $20; four normal territories plus the Factory count as seven territories and add $21; 13 resources make six pairs and add $12. These categories add $53 to held coins. Add the selected structure bonus too; it is earned even if enemies control the territories containing your structures, with the payout depending on the selected tile and qualifying features. Victory goes to the most total coins; ties break by workers + mechs + structures (not character), then power, popularity, resources controlled, territories controlled, and stars placed.
answers.evidence: Scoring table at popularity 7–12 gives $4 per star, $3 per territory and $2 per pair; Factory counts as three territories; example shows $53. Structure bonus is earned even if enemies control structures' territories; listed tiebreak sequence follows total coins.
